definition: The practice of deliberately probing an AI system for vulnerabilities, harmful outputs, or failure modes, typically before deployment.
details: Red teaming — whether performed by internal teams, external experts, or automated adversarial systems — is a key part of responsible AI development, surfacing risks like harmful content generation, bias, or susceptibility to jailbreaks.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. Boil it down and it is this: The practice of deliberately probing an AI system for vulnerabilities, harmful outputs, or failure modes, typically before deployment. Here is why it matters: Red teaming — whether performed by internal teams, external experts, or automated adversarial systems — is a key part of responsible AI development, surfacing risks like harmful content generation, bias, or susceptibility to jailbreaks. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Red Teaming.
